newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iraq's military weakness strengthens Iran.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's military weakness strengthens Iran.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) on Saturday said Iraq's weakness has created a military imbalance and increased threats by arch-rival Iran against Gulf states.

"Iraq's inability to exercise self defence has created a strategic and military imbalance in the region," UAE Foreign Minister Rashid Abdullah Al-Nuaimi was quoted by the state-run Emirates News Agency (WAM) as saying. Iraq and Iran fought eight years of war which ended in 1988.
But Iraq's military capabilities have been badly hit following its invasion of Kuwait, the 1990-1991 Gulf War against U.S.-led allied troops and the imposition of U.N. sanctions.
Al-Nuaimi said Iran has deployed offensive weapons at three Gulf islands of Greater Tunb, Lesser Tunb and Abu Musa, the center of a territorial dispute between the UAE and non-Arab neighbouring Iran.
"As long as there are states in the region with greed, flexing their muscles, and using maneuvres and threats, there will be no trust nor any cooperation," he said.
"Iran has deployed offensive weapons directed at all Gulf Arab states," added al-Nuaimi.
Iran began on Thursday a 10-day air and sea exercise in the Gulf region.
Al-Nuaimi, who was speaking to Arab journalists in Abu Dhabi, said the UAE wants a peaceful solution to the territorial dispute with Iran over the three Gulf islands.
Al-Nuaimi's statement was a rare public accusation by the UAE to Iran as a threat to the oil-rich Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states, which groups Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar and Oman.
GCC states have expressed their concern over Iran's rearmamment programme, including the deployment of submarines and missiles.

Iran, which has repeatedly said its rearmament was only for self-defence purposes, is the only Gulf state to deploy submarines in the Gulf region which has about 70 percent of the world's oil reserves.
